## v1.4.0

### Attention emphasis in Settings

- Settings now has a dedicated section for attention emphasis: it shows which signals push a repository up the queue and lets you weight them.
- The section is explicit about its scope — emphasis only. It changes the queue order; the health score and its checks do not move.
- Every control states its effect, and the estimates shown are derived from the same weights the scoring uses, so the preview cannot drift from the result.

### A generic handle on the public site

- The public site no longer previews a personal handle. It renders a generic sample fleet (`acme`) instead, with repositories, alerts and pull requests that illustrate the queue without exposing anyone's account.
- The hero gained a pressure field that reacts to the sample scores, plus a legend that reads the field instead of leaving it as decoration.
- The queue cards, inspector, scoring and runtimes sections were rebuilt around that sample fleet, so the whole page tells one consistent story.

### Theme

- The app follows the operating system preference on first load, with no flash of the wrong theme.
- The footer toggle is now icon-only and remembers an explicit choice over the auto-detected one.

### Accessibility and contrast

- Pass over the design tokens: neutral status pills, switches, banners and the rail were retouched to raise text contrast without flattening the hierarchy.
- Some surfaces are still below AA and are known follow-ups: buttons in the 3.0–3.7 range, status text over surface, accent chips, banners and the rail. They are listed rather than hidden.
